title: Protocol PRT-TS-001 -- A Phase 3 study of TSX-101 in Metastatic breast cancer
text:
- Phase: Phase 3
- Planned sample size: 908 participants
- Primary endpoint: Change from baseline in the primary efficacy measure for Metastatic breast cancer at week 24
- Visit window: +/-7 days
- Screening period: 28 days
- SAE reporting to sponsor: within 24 hours
- Informed consent form version: 1.0
- eCRF data entry: within 5 days of visit
- Query resolution: within 10 business days
- Independent DSMB: Yes
- Key exclusions: Participation in another interventional study within 30 days; Clinically significant laboratory abnormality at screening

title: SOP-001 Informed Consent
text: Defines how informed consent is obtained, documented and refreshed for all interventional studies.

title: SOP-001 Informed Consent
text: Only the IRB/EC-approved consent version listed in the protocol may be used. Rule IC-1: the protocol must reference an approved consent form version of 2.0 or higher for any amended protocol.

title: SOP-001 Informed Consent
text: Rule IC-2: when an amendment changes risks, procedures or visit burden, active participants must be re-consented within 30 days of IRB approval of the amendment.

title: SOP-002 Safety Reporting
text: Sets timelines for reporting adverse events to the sponsor safety desk.

title: SOP-002 Safety Reporting
text: Rule SR-1: investigators must report every serious adverse event (SAE) to the sponsor within 24 hours of awareness. Protocols must not specify a longer window.

title: SOP-002 Safety Reporting
text: Fatal or life-threatening SUSARs are expedited to regulators within 7 calendar days; all other SUSARs within 15.

title: SOP-003 Visit Windows and Scheduling
text: Limits how far a protocol visit may drift from its nominal day.

title: SOP-003 Visit Windows and Scheduling
text: Rule VW-1: Phase 1 protocols may allow at most +/-3 days. Rule VW-2: Phase 2 and Phase 3 protocols may allow at most +/-7 days for treatment-period visits.

title: SOP-003 Visit Windows and Scheduling
text: An out-of-window visit is a protocol deviation and must be logged within 5 business days.

title: SOP-004 Eligibility and Screening
text: Controls the screening period and escalation of high screen-failure rates.

title: SOP-004 Eligibility and Screening
text: Rule ES-1: the screening period must not exceed 28 days from consent to randomization.

title: SOP-004 Eligibility and Screening
text: Rule ES-2: a site whose screen-failure rate exceeds 40% after 10 or more screened participants triggers an eligibility-criteria review with the medical monitor.

title: SOP-005 Clinical Data Management
text: Sets timeliness expectations for electronic case report form (eCRF) data.

title: SOP-005 Clinical Data Management
text: Rule DM-1: visit data must be entered in the eCRF within 5 days of the visit.

title: SOP-005 Clinical Data Management
text: Rule DM-2: data queries must be resolved within 10 business days; protocols may not relax this.

title: SOP-006 Site Selection and Performance Management
text: Defines objective site performance thresholds and remediation.

title: SOP-006 Site Selection and Performance Management
text: Rule SP-1: a site enrolling fewer than 0.5 participants per month after its first 3 active months enters a remediation plan.

title: SOP-006 Site Selection and Performance Management
text: Rule SP-2: more than 5 protocol deviations per 10 enrolled participants, or average query age above 15 days, triggers a for-cause monitoring visit.

title: SOP-007 Protocol Amendments
text: Governs how protocol amendments are classified, approved and implemented.

title: SOP-007 Protocol Amendments
text: Rule PA-1: substantial amendments (changes to endpoints, sample size >10%, eligibility or safety monitoring) require IRB/EC approval before implementation and notification of the DSMB if one exists.

title: SOP-007 Protocol Amendments
text: Rule PA-2: every Phase 3 protocol must name an independent Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB).

title: SOP-008 Data Privacy and AI Tool Use
text: Protects participant privacy when using analytics and AI assistants.

title: SOP-008 Data Privacy and AI Tool Use
text: Participant names, contact details, medical record numbers and dates of birth must never be entered into AI assistants. Use coded participant IDs only.

title: SOP-008 Data Privacy and AI Tool Use
text: AI assistants may summarize aggregate operational data and policies. They must not provide medical advice, dosing recommendations for individual patients, or unblind treatment assignments.
